issues.title: Abstract overstates coercivity-proof coverage

failure_location.quote:
Additionally, we develop coercive formulations based on Nitsche's method,
        and provide proofs of coercivity for all new and key existing approximations.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: these suggest two core ideas for constructing approximations for the Poisson problem with $D=1$ and Dirichlet boundary conditions.

However, we are unable to comment about coercivity of this method but
in \cref{section:Nitsche} we will derive a new method that is coercive.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims that the paper provides coercivity proofs for every new and key existing approximation. The body identifies DDM1 and DDM2 as the two core existing ideas, yet after defining DDM2 explicitly states that it is unable to comment on that method's coercivity and instead develops a new coercive replacement. The paper therefore supports proofs for selected existing or modified methods, not all key existing approximations.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract materially overstates the breadth of the paper's theoretical coverage, although this does not by itself invalidate any individual method.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Narrow the abstract to state that coercivity is proved for all new formulations and for only some selected approximations from the literature; DDM2 must remain outside the coverage claim unless a coercivity proof is supplied.
issues.why_classification: The body presents DDM2 as a core existing approximation but expressly declines to establish its coercivity. Narrowing the abstract is a contained repair with no formal dependent chain, but it withdraws the coherent advertised promise of coverage for all key existing approximations. A recognizably comparable coverage claim survives with only limited loss, so the issue is moderate rather than minor or serious.

issues.title: DDM1 theorem states an off-diagonal coercivity bound

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $D := D(x) \geq d > 0$ is a scalar function.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims a(u,v)≥c||u||², which fails at v=0 for every nonzero u. Its method definition and proof context support only diagonal coercivity: using D≥d>0 gives a(u,u)≥d||u||².
issues.overall_effect: The printed theorem is literally false, although its intended and subsequently used diagonal coercivity conclusion is immediately recoverable under the existing assumptions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the displayed off-diagonal inequality by the diagonal coercivity estimate a(u,u) ≥ C‖u‖²; under the existing assumption D ≥ d > 0, one may take C=d for the stated weighted norm.
issues.why_classification: The term “coercive,” the method definition, and the proof’s calculation uniquely force a(u,u). The literal a(u,v) claim is contradicted by v=0, but correcting v to u requires no new inference, assumption, or dependent repair and preserves the intended theorem exactly.

issues.title: SBM coercivity proof compares nonidentical norms

failure_location.quote: This is identical, up to epsilon scalling, to DDM1,

issues.failure_explanation: The quadratic form computed in the proof contains |∇(φu)|², whereas eq:sbmnorm and the cited DDM1 norm contain φ|∇u|². Since ∇(φu)=φ∇u+u∇φ, this is not an epsilon rescaling, and the cited DDM1 result does not prove coercivity in the printed SBM norm.
issues.overall_effect: Coercivity of SBM in the specifically printed norm is unestablished, and the later stabilized-advection theorem imports that diffusion coercivity. The SBM formulation itself is not thereby invalidated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the printed SBM norm by the energy norm ‖u‖²_SBM = ∫_B(|∇(φu)|²+ε⁻²(1−φ)|u|²) dx, verify that it is a norm, and conclude a(u,u) ≥ d‖u‖²_SBM. Use this same diffusion norm in the dependent stabilized-advection theorem; its advection argument then remains valid because the added terms are nonnegative.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes a genuine invalid identification: |∇(φu)|² is not an epsilon rescaling of φ|∇u|². The energy-norm replacement is a contained, source-supported repair and preserves comparable coercivity results for both SBM and its stabilized-advection extension, but it changes the coherent norm-specific guarantee originally stated. That limited mathematical loss exceeds a minor repair without requiring global reconstruction.

issues.title: Tentative-velocity subproblem constrains the wrong variable
issues.failure_explanation: The executable subproblem has tilde u as its unknown, while the boundary instruction says u=g. Because u and tilde u are distinguished throughout the time-stepping formula, the boundary line does not specify boundary data for the unknown being solved.
issues.overall_effect: As printed, the first IPC subproblem is not fully specified for its tentative-velocity unknown; the surrounding Navier–Stokes procedure requires the intended reading to be executable.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the boundary condition in the tentative-velocity subproblem to tilde u = g on ∂Ω, adding the same time index as the tentative unknown if indices are displayed.
issues.why_classification: The surrounding sentence says that the subproblem is solved for the tentative velocity, and every differential term uses that unknown while u is separately distinguished. Thus the boundary variable has one uniquely forced transcriptional correction, which fully specifies the subproblem without changing the algorithm or any guarantee.
